tasks.description:
Create orchestrator/phase_idle_budget.py with a PhaseIdleBudgetTimer
class. Owns DEFAULT_PHASE_IDLE_BUDGET_MIN = 30 (parity with
consensus_wrapper.py:59); state (pipeline_id, phase, last_spawn_at,
last_alert_at, per_role_last_action); APIs record_spawn(pipeline_id,
phase, role, action), check(now, pending_hitl_count), reset. Emits
stuck-phase-transition once at the 1x threshold and once at 2x via the
same overseer-alert entry point overseer/monitor.py uses. HITL-pending
suppression (AC-R13): when pending_hitl_count>0 the 1x alert downgrades
to priority=low with pending_hitl_ids in reason and the 2x alert is
suppressed. Every alert carries a structured per_role_state payload
field (AC-R4) derived from per_role_last_action. Idempotent re-fire
within a threshold bucket.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- File exists; class exposes record_spawn, check, reset; constant == 30.
- Unit tests: 0 idle min -> no emit; 30 min -> 1x emit once with
  populated per_role_state; 60 min -> 2x emit once (1x not re-emitted);
  record_spawn resets and updates per-role state; idempotent across
  check() calls in the same bucket; pending_hitl_count=1 at 30 min ->
  priority=low + pending HITL id in reason; pending_hitl_count=1 at
  60 min -> no additional alert.

tasks.description:
Wire PhaseIdleBudgetTimer.check(now, pending_hitl_count) into the

tick reads the pending-HITL count (routes/decisions.py open-decision

structured phase_idle_budget_tick log once per emitted alert.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Tick invokes check exactly once per loop iteration.
- After the fixture advances past 30 min with no record_spawn and zero
  pending HITL, the overseer alert handler is invoked exactly once with
  anomaly="stuck-phase-transition", priority=medium.
- With one pending HITL the same interval emits priority=low and the
  pending HITL id appears in reason.

tasks.description:
Create orchestrator/on_demand_spawner.py with an OnDemandSpawner class.
Holds refs to KubernetesSpawner, PhaseIdleBudgetTimer, the
OrchestratorSessionKeepAlive, and the GatewayClient. tick(pipeline_id,
phase, roles): per role, calls derive_next_action -> wait/complete: no
spawn; confirm/propose/ack/nack: compose_event_prompt in-process then
spawn_event. record_phase_start(pipeline_id, phase, roles, slice_id?)
does per-role wiring (BLOCKER 2 & 3): register the gateway session once
per (pipeline, role) via GatewayClient.register_session (lifted from
kubernetes_spawner.py:761-794), register the token with the keep-alive,
pre-warm the per-role worktree PVC, and register the consensus tracker
entry idempotently. record_phase_end deletes sessions + unregisters
keep-alive.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Class exists with tick/record_phase_start/record_phase_end.
- Unit: wait -> no spawn; propose -> spawn with role+composed
  prompt+model decision; confirm -> same path; record_phase_start calls
  register_session once per role with expected kwargs, captures token,
  forwards to keep-alive; re-entry of tick doesn't double-spawn while a
  spawn is in flight; 10 events in <100ms -> 1 spawn (coalesced, TASK-2-9);
  record_phase_end calls delete_session + unregister per role; tracker
  registration idempotent vs spawn_all.

before the phase-completion check. Phase-end hook: call
OnDemandSpawner.record_phase_end at phase transition. After this, the
orchestrator is the only path emitting BRC verbs (wrapper passive).

tasks.description:
Per-role single-pod-in-flight precondition (AC-R1 + AC-R8). RWO per-role
PVCs (architect Q1) mean only one pod per (pipeline, role) can hold the
mount; a second concurrent spawn would silently hang. Orchestrator-side
coalescer: OnDemandSpawner.tick records in_flight: set[(pipeline_id, role)];
while a spawn is in flight, subsequent derive_next_action returns are
coalesced; the flag clears when the Job reaches a terminal phase (existing
pod-watch path). Spawner-side precondition:
KubernetesSpawner.spawn_agent_job raises SpawnPreconditionError if a
non-terminal Job already exists for the same (pipeline, role) label
selector (defense-in-depth).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- NACK fan-out: 10 actionable events for the same role in <100ms -> exactly
  one spawn, nine coalesced.
- Precondition: with job.status.active=1 mocked, spawn_agent_job raises
  SpawnPreconditionError and does not call create_job.
- Cross-role independence: two roles' in-flight spawns do not block each
  other.

tasks.description:
Orphan-commit detector (AC-R6, architect Q3 = land here). A pod can exit
after `git commit M` but before its propose/ack/nack finishes, leaving
commits with no BRC verb. A new OrphanCommitDetector runs once per
OnDemandSpawner.tick BEFORE derive_next_action for a role: read the role's
last_reviewed_commit_sha from .egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md,
call gateway_client.git_log_range(base=sha, head=branch), cross-reference
tracker.events_for_role(role); if commits exist with no covering
CONSENSUS_PROPOSE, emit OVERSEER_ALERT(anomaly="orphan_commit_post_spawn")
and re-spawn the role with a prompt instructing it to propose covering
exactly those commits (no new code work).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Integration: simulate pod exit after commit but before propose ->
  detector emits the alert and re-spawns with the orphan-recovery prompt.
- No-op when commits are covered by a BRC verb.
- No-op when there are no new commits on the role's branch.

tasks.description:
Atomic brc-memory writes (AC-R12). The durable BRC memory at

Cross-references the TASK-2-9 single-pod precondition.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:

  simultaneous writes and confirms the final file is one complete write,
  never a partial concatenation.
- Cross-reference: TASK-2-9(b) covers the spawner-side single-pod
  precondition.

tasks.description:
Tolerant pod-state reader for cross-version revert (AC-R7, robustness
fall-through). After this PR merges, in-flight pipelines may have
on-demand pods or no pod at all between events; a reverted orchestrator's
startup reconciliation must not crash on a missing wrapper. In
orchestrator/startup_reconciliation.py + the restart-on-resume path in
routes/pipelines.py, add a fall-through: when no Job with the role label
is Running for a (pipeline, role) AND the BRC tracker has a non-empty
event history for that role, treat the pipeline as "on-demand in-flight"
and re-derive next-action instead of marking it failed; document the
revert scenario inline.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- Integration: start a pipeline on the new code, run a few BRC events
  through on-demand, simulate the revert by importing the previous-version
  reconciliation function alongside a frozen on-demand tracker state; the
  reader completes without raising and the pipeline re-enters the run loop
  without marking any role FAILED.
- The same reader against a synthetic legacy long-lived wrapper-pod state
  continues to work (no regression).

decisions.question: What is the acceptable cold-start latency budget for a per-event pod spawn (from `_derive_next_action != "wait"` to the agent process running)?

options.label: ≤ 3 s p95 — tight budget; requires worktree-PVC pre-warm AND gateway-session reuse (Option A's full optimization)
≤ 8 s p95 — loose budget; allows per-spawn gateway-session setup (worktree still pre-warmed); simpler orchestrator state but slower per-event cycle
≤ 20 s p95 — generous; would allow Option D (fresh PVC + fresh session per spawn) at the cost of a measurably slower BRC cycle
No fixed budget — measure-then-decide post-rollout, gated on a kill-switch flag
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "No fixed cold-start latency requirement — this is a resource-freeing change, not latency-sensitive. Per-phase reuse of the prompt-cache prefix, gateway session, and worktree is unchanged; only the wait moves out of the pod, so no cold-start SLO gates the change."}

decisions.question: How should the gateway session be managed across a role's successive on-demand spawns? (Today a long-lived pod holds one session via 30 s heartbeat; under on-demand spawning the orchestrator must take over session lifecycle.)

options.label: Per-role session held by the orchestrator for the whole phase, refreshed by an orchestrator-side keep-alive (mirrors today's lifecycle but moves the heartbeat emitter; reuses today's gateway/session_manager.py semantics)
Fresh session per spawn (simpler orchestrator state, more gateway log noise, pays credential resolve every event)
Orchestrator-wide session multiplexed across all roles (smallest gateway-side footprint, but breaks today's per-role audit and per-role model routing from #2769)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Per-role session held by the orchestrator for the whole phase, refreshed by an orchestrator-side keep-alive (mirrors today's lifecycle but moves the heartbeat emitter; reuses today's gateway/session_manager.py semantics)"}

decisions.question: Under on-demand spawning, who owns the "no actionable event for X minutes" idle-budget overseer alert that today fires from inside the wrapper at the 30-min EGG_BRC_IDLE_BUDGET_MIN? (Operator-visible signal — `stuck-phase-transition` anomaly tag at 1× and 2× thresholds.)

options.label: Orchestrator-side per-role timer that emits the same anomaly tag with the same thresholds (drop-in replacement; operator UX unchanged)
Replace with a phase-level 'no spawns for X minutes' alert at the orchestrator (different signal — fires once per phase regardless of role count, simpler to operate but loses per-role granularity)
Drop the idle-budget alert entirely; rely on the existing phase-timeout SLO (smallest code, weakest signal)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Replace with a phase-level 'no spawns for X minutes' alert at the orchestrator (different signal — fires once per phase regardless of role count, simpler to operate but loses per-role granularity)"}

decisions.question: What is the rollout shape? The change touches spawn / run / terminate paths simultaneously; a behind-flag rollout lets operators flip per pipeline / per phase during burn-in, while a big-bang rollout matches #2908's "no env-flag rollback, revert by git" stance.

options.label: Feature-flagged per-pipeline (e.g. PipelineConfig.on_demand_spawn=True/False, default False initially, flip to True after burn-in) — operator can pin a known-good pipeline to the long-lived model while the on-demand path soaks elsewhere
Feature-flagged per-phase (e.g. enable for refine only first, since it has the lowest event volume and the cleanest cache hit pattern) — graduated rollout per phase
Big-bang with rollback-by-git-revert (mirrors #2908 slice-4 stance) — smallest config surface, requires a clean revert path in the PR
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Big-bang with rollback-by-git-revert (mirrors #2908 slice-4 stance) — smallest config surface, requires a clean revert path in the PR"}

decisions.question: What is the retirement scope for `orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py` after on-demand spawning is the default? Today the wrapper does five things (event loop, heartbeat, idle budget, agent invocation, signal/SIGTERM cleanup); under Option A the first three move to the orchestrator and agent invocation collapses to a single exec.

options.label: Delete consensus_wrapper.py entirely; the pod entrypoint becomes `python3 -m egg_agent --model X --max-turns N` with the composed prompt on stdin (smallest in-pod surface)

Keep a thin one-shot wrapper that handles only signal trapping + heartbeat-once-on-start + agent invocation (preserves the kubelet SIGTERM contract that today's wrapper handles via the cleanup trap at consensus_wrapper.py:117-124)
Keep the full wrapper but skip the loop when an EGG_ON_DEMAND=1 env var is set (graceful migration with both paths coexisting until burn-in completes; doubles the test surface)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Delete consensus_wrapper.py entirely; the pod entrypoint becomes `python3 -m egg_agent --model X --max-turns N` with the composed prompt on stdin (smallest in-pod surface)"}

decisions.question: Are overseer agents (decision-maker, advisor — see orchestrator/overseer/monitor.py) in scope for on-demand spawning, or out of scope for this change? They have a different lifecycle today (spawned by overseer/monitor.py on an anomaly + periodic cadence, not via concurrent_executor.spawn_all) and are already arguably on-demand.

options.label: Out of scope — leave overseer agent lifecycle as-is; this issue is about BRC-loop roles only

In scope — unify the spawn path so overseer agents go through the same OnDemandSpawner (cleaner long-term shape, more diff in this PR, may require fixing edge cases the overseer's bespoke path already solved)
In scope, but as a follow-up issue — note the unification target in this issue's closeout but defer the work
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "In scope, but as a follow-up issue — note the unification target in this issue's closeout but defer the work"}

decisions.question: Documenter has zero assigned tasks in slice-1 of issue-3023 (all three slice-1 tasks have role=null). Documenter's only assignment is task-3-4 in slice-3, which is premature because the slice-1 coder branch has not committed any implementation yet. The documenter producer branch is at origin/main with zero commits ahead, so v1 and v2 BRC proposals were empty and reviewer_code (correctly) NACKed v2. How should slice-1's BRC matrix unblock?

options.label: Skip documenter for slice-1 and slice-2 — defer documenter participation until slice-3 (when task-3-4 has substrate to document); remove documenter from the slice-1/slice-2 BRC matrix or mark not-required
Assign at least one slice-1 documentation task to documenter (e.g. a doc-stub for orchestrator/phase_idle_budget.py or a slice-1 runbook snippet) so the producer has legitimate work to propose
Keep documenter blocking and have it withdraw its current proposal; let the BRC cycle stay open until slice-3 — accept the idle-budget alert risk
Defer slice-1 entirely until plan refinement re-scopes documenter coverage across all three slices

pr.title: On-demand agent spawning: orchestrator-owned event loop, no idle pods (#3023)
pr.description:
Invert the BRC agent lifecycle. Today the orchestrator spawns the full
team at phase start and each pod runs a long-lived in-pod event-pump bash
loop (`orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py`) that long-polls the bus and
invokes the agent one-shot per event, staying alive (idle, heartbeating,
holding a gateway session) for the whole phase. This PR lifts the wait out
of the pods into the orchestrator as a single blocking thread covering all
agents: the orchestrator derives per-role actionability with
`_derive_next_action` and spawns a one-shot pod only when a role has an
actionable event; the pod handles the event and exits. No idle pods.

Per-phase reuse of the prompt-cache prefix, gateway session, and worktree
is UNCHANGED — the orchestrator now holds the per-(pipeline, role) session
alive and reuses the per-role worktree PVC across spawns. Resolves the
refine HITL decisions: cq-1 no cold-start SLO (resource-freeing, not
latency-gated); cq-2 orchestrator-held per-role session; cq-3 phase-level
"no spawns for X min" idle alert (same stuck-phase-transition tag/threshold);
cq-4 big-bang, rollback-by-git-revert; cq-5 delete consensus_wrapper.py
entirely; cq-6 overseer agents out of scope (follow-up issue).

Three dependent slices, single PR: (1) orchestrator-side phase-level
idle-budget alert; (2) the on-demand spawner + per-(pipeline, role)
worktree-PVC and gateway-session reuse, with the still-spawned wrapper pod
made passive via env guards so exactly one path emits BRC verbs; (3)
consensus_wrapper.py retirement + entrypoint simplification to
`python3 -m egg_agent`.
pr.test_plan:
Automated (`make test` is changeset-aware; `make test-all` for CI ground truth):
- Unit: PhaseIdleBudgetTimer, OnDemandSpawner (mocked spawner+tracker),
  OrchestratorSessionKeepAlive (mocked gateway), KubernetesSpawner
  create_on_demand_spawn_fn (mocked k8s API), derive_next_action
  in-process/route parity.
- Integration: orchestrator run loop drives one full BRC cycle
  (propose -> ack -> confirm) for a role, asserting one spawn per
  actionable event, zero spawns on wait, bare `python3 -m egg_agent`
  command (no `bash -c`), per-spawn log retention, and the phase-level
  idle alert at 30 min of no spawns.
- Restart resilience: orchestrator restart mid-phase; reconstruct-from-
  messages fallback (routes/consensus.py:111-154) still works; the tick
  re-derives next-action and spawns whatever was actionable; session
  keep-alive re-populated.
- No BRC behaviour change: per-event prompt byte-identical to the
  wrapper-rendered prompt for the same (role, event_payload); prefix-cache
  hit rate preserved (LiteLLM cost/cache logger).

Manual (reviewer):
- `make test` and `make lint` green.
- Before/after grep for consensus_wrapper / build_consensus_wrapped_command
  / EVENT_PUMP_ shows zero production matches post-slice-3.
pr.manual_steps:
Pre-merge: none.

Post-merge (operator drain-then-revert protocol; cq-4 big-bang has no
feature flag, so a revert must drain in-flight pipelines first):
  egg-orch pipeline list --running
  # For each running pipeline:
  #   - if it can finish in <T hours, let it run to completion
  #   - else: egg-orch pipeline cancel <id> --reason "pre-revert drain"
  # Then `git revert` the commit on main; the reverted orchestrator's
  # pod-state reader (TASK-3-5) tolerates either lifecycle so freshly
  # spawned pipelines work.
File the cq-6 overseer-unification follow-up issue and the spawn_all
rename follow-up issue; link both from the PR closeout.

questions.question: What is the concrete resource-saving target operators care about? (e.g. 'halve the idle-pod-minutes per phase', 'support 10x current concurrent pipelines on the same k3s node', 'reduce per-phase memory reservation by X%'). This shapes how aggressively the acceptance test must drive the cold-start budget down vs. accept a higher latency for a cleaner code shape.
questions.answer: No specific numeric target. The goal is qualitative: idle pods (a role blocked in `wait`) should not exist, so their CPU/memory reservation, pinned gateway session, and 30s heartbeat overhead are freed during waits. This is a resource-freeing change, NOT a latency optimization — do not gate it on a cold-start SLO (see cq-1). Critically: per-phase reuse of the prompt-cache prefix, gateway session, and worktree is UNCHANGED. The only thing that moves is the wait — out of the pods and into the orchestrator, as a single blocking thread covering all agents (one wait that wakes when any role becomes actionable), not N per-pod waits and not per-role timers.

questions.question: Are there any pipelines or repos currently relying on the in-pod wrapper's debug-shell-able-ness during incidents? (e.g. `kubectl exec` into a stuck wrapper, inspect the heartbeat subshell, read AGENT_OUTPUT_LOG). If so the on-demand model loses that affordance — would a per-spawn pod log retained in .egg-state/ be a sufficient replacement, or do operators need a long-lived debug shim?
questions.answer: Not a blocker and not a reason to keep a long-lived pod. The orchestrator's existing per-container log capture, retained per spawn, should suffice for incident inspection. We don't believe operators rely on `kubectl exec` into a live wrapper's heartbeat subshell. If that affordance turns out to matter in practice, address it as a separate, lightweight concern (e.g. a retained per-spawn log) — don't preserve the idle pod for it.

questions.question: The plan will rely on per-role worktree PVCs already being reusable across multiple spawns. Is there any in-flight work (#2866 k3s-as-sole-runtime, #3017 declarative phase/stage abstraction) that is about to change the PVC lifecycle or the spawner's worktree-mount pattern in a way the plan should anchor on?
questions.answer: Anchor on the current per-role worktree-mount pattern in kubernetes_spawner.py — it already supports worktree reuse across spawns, which is exactly what this change needs. #2866 (k3s as sole runtime) is about removing the Docker runtime, not changing the k8s PVC/worktree-mount pattern, so no conflict. #3017 (declarative phase/stage abstraction) is the one to coordinate with: it reshapes the phase model that this change also touches (spawn/run/terminate per phase). Neither is changing the PVC lifecycle imminently, so proceed on today's pattern and flag #3017 as the adjacency to keep in view.

questions.question: The issue references #2958 (streaming per-task commits / producer lifecycle) as adjacent. Does the on-demand spawner need to coexist with a producer that 'keeps working' across multiple commits in one logical session, or does the per-event spawn model assume one event approximately equals one commit / one BRC verb cleanly?
questions.answer: Do NOT assume one-event ≈ one-commit rigidly. A spawned pod runs the full agent invocation to completion of that event's unit of work, which may produce multiple commits in a single invocation — this is exactly #2958's streaming/producer-keeps-working model. The pod exits when the agent finishes its turn for that event, not after one commit. So the model is one-spawn-per-actionable-event where a spawn may yield N commits; the orchestrator's single wait then wakes on the next actionable event (e.g. reviewers' delta-review of the streamed commits) after the pod exits. This composes cleanly with #2958.

questions.question: The current 30-min EGG_BRC_IDLE_BUDGET_MIN was tuned for the in-pod wrapper (consensus_wrapper.py:52-58 comment). Once the orchestrator owns the equivalent timer, is there appetite to tighten or widen it (e.g. tighten to 10 min now that there's no risk of a wrapper-side false positive, or widen to 60 min to match the prefix-cache TTL so we don't alert on legitimately-idle phases that are still within cache window)?
questions.answer: Keep the current threshold semantics; do not retune as part of this change. The 30-min EGG_BRC_IDLE_BUDGET_MIN moves to the orchestrator as the phase-level idle alert (cq-3) with the same threshold and the same stuck-phase-transition anomaly tag, so operator UX does not regress. Retuning — tightening toward the WS7-observed 10-13min legitimate-idle ceiling, or widening toward the ≥60min prefix-cache TTL — is a separable follow-up once the orchestrator-side timer has soaked. Don't bundle it here.
